title: Physical reinsertion and the strong-coupling boundary
analyticalQuestion: How does the physically lifted enhanced-dissipation branch change the one-carrier window, and which parts survive multi-carrier superposition?
supportedTakeaway: The one-carrier enhanced-dissipation branch changes the normalized numerator from epsilon^(7/3) to epsilon^(11/6) and enlarges the scale window from R^(2/3) log R to R^(4/3) (log R)^2. The result is unconditional only for the declared one-carrier family, remains insufficient at fixed R and arbitrarily large coupling, and extends to multiple carriers only under a full-superposition integrated enhanced-dissipation hypothesis with constants uniform over the compared family.
analyticClaims: The R0.72N raw one-carrier cubic is exactly the R0.72L cubic row after parabolic rescaling.
After multiplication by Theta and division by D^(1/3), the square-root raw cubic produces the normalized numerator epsilon^(11/6).
The exact-root correction is paid by the one-carrier semigroup operator norm and does not destroy the square-root cubic bound.
The one-carrier window is sqrt(epsilon) less than or comparable to R^(2/3) L_(R,epsilon), equivalently epsilon less than or comparable to R^(4/3) L_(R,epsilon)^2.
At fixed R, the current upper envelope is of order sqrt(epsilon)/log(epsilon) and therefore does not close arbitrarily strong coupling.

For more than one carrier, the p-dependent window is conditional on an integrated estimate for the full superposition with constants uniform over the compared parameter and geometry family, not on carrierwise bounds.
finiteDiagnostics: Producer and independent exact-arithmetic audits evaluate the same four R values, two regimes, and three relative coupling levels.
Panel thresholds suppress unknown absolute theorem constants and visualize scale laws rather than certified numerical closure constants.
No PDE evolution, regression, interpolation, or fitted exponent is run by the figure package.
The two-carrier flat critical point is an exact theorem-applicability obstruction, not a counterexample to a full-superposition estimate.

panelClaims.A: The old and enhanced-dissipation one-carrier window scales are compared with constants suppressed; audit anchors verify exponent bookkeeping.
panelClaims.B: At fixed R, the algebraic enhanced-dissipation screen improves the old screen but eventually exceeds the scale-one guide, so the present payment is not an arbitrary-coupling closure.
panelClaims.C: The filled blue point is the proved N=1 case. The ochre open dashed p-dependent curve is conditional for every multi-carrier configuration and assumes uniform full-superposition enhanced-dissipation constants over the plotted family, including p near one.
panelClaims.D: An exact two-carrier common-band profile has cubic rather than quadratic departure at a critical point, so common-band support does not imply uniform Morse geometry.

renderPolicy.proved: blue solid line or filled circle
renderPolicy.conditional: ochre dashed line with open square markers

claimBoundary: The unconditional theorem concerns only the declared fixed-background, phase-aligned, row-aligned, exact-root-corrected one-carrier triangular 2.5D family. The multi-carrier curve assumes a full-superposition integrated enhanced-dissipation estimate with constants uniform over the plotted parameter and geometry family. The figure does not prove fixed-R arbitrary-coupling closure, logarithmic cubic growth, multiscale absorption, a general three-dimensional continuation criterion, finite-time singularity, or global Navier-Stokes regularity.
